_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Croatia covering Illyrian/Roman Dalmatia, Croatian kingdom (Tomislav, first king 925), personal union with Hungary 1102, Ottoman threat (Antemurale Christianitatis), Habsburg Military Frontier (Vojna Krajina), Illyrian Movement (19th century national awakening), Triune Kingdom, South Slav movement, Kingdom of Yugoslavia, NDH (Ustaše fascist puppet state 1941-45, Jasenovac concentration camp), Tito's Partisans, Croatian Spring 1971, independence 1991, Croatian War of Independence 1991-95 (Operation Storm), Tudjman, EU accession 2013, eurozone/Schengen 2023.

religion.note: Strongly Catholic (identity marker separating Croats from Orthodox Serbs and Muslim Bosniaks); Catholicism = Croatness; Vatican close ally; religious practice moderate; Orthodox minority (Serb)

ethnic_groups.name: Croatian
ethnic_groups.notes: South Slavic; Catholic identity; Latin script (vs Serbian Cyrillic); strong national consciousness; Western-oriented (Habsburg/Venetian heritage); large diaspora (Germany, Australia, Americas)

ethnic_groups.name: Serbian
ethnic_groups.notes: Orthodox; pre-war 12.2% (1991); reduced by war/exodus (Operation Storm 1995, ~200,000 fled); Krajina region; return incomplete; political reconciliation ongoing

ethnic_groups.name: Italian
ethnic_groups.notes: Istria/Dalmatia; historical Venetian communities; bilingual education

ethnic_groups.name: Hungarian
ethnic_groups.notes: Eastern Slavonia/Baranja; historical minority; bilingual areas

ethnic_groups.name: Other
ethnic_groups.notes: Roma (~17k), Czech, Slovak, Rusyn, Albanian, Montenegrin

country_profile.notes_unique: Antemurale Christianitatis ('Bulwark of Christendom', defended Europe from Ottoman expansion); Dubrovnik (UNESCO, 'Pearl of the Adriatic', Republic of Ragusa independent 1358-1808, Game of Thrones); Diocletian's Palace (Split, UNESCO, Roman emperor); 1,244 islands (1,777 km coastline, Adriatic); NDH/Ustaše (fascist puppet state 1941-45, Jasenovac concentration camp, tens of thousands killed); Croatian War of Independence 1991-95 (Vukovar siege, Operation Storm); Tudjman (first president, controversial nationalist); Euro/Schengen January 2023 (only country to join both simultaneously); necktie invented in Croatia (cravat from 'Croat'); Nikola Tesla (born ethnic Serb in Croatia, contested); water polo/handball sporting culture

current_leader.name: Andrej Plenković
current_leader.title: Prime Minister
current_leader.notes: HDZ (Croatian Democratic Union); EU diplomat turned PM; moderate conservative; euro/Schengen accession; three terms; EU integration champion; stable

head_of_state.name: Zoran Milanović
head_of_state.title: President
head_of_state.notes: SDP; former PM (2011-16); populist as president; feuds with PM Plenković; controversial constitutional confrontations; seeks re-election

former_leaders.name: Kolinda Grabar-Kitarović
former_leaders.notes: HDZ; first female president; NATO assistant secretary general; nationalist-populist; lost re-election to Milanović

former_leaders.name: Ivo Sanader
former_leaders.notes: HDZ; EU accession negotiations; resigned abruptly; convicted corruption (10 years prison); major political scandal

former_leaders.name: Stjepan Mesić
former_leaders.notes: Moderate; last president of Yugoslavia (briefly); democratic transition; war crimes cooperation with ICTY

former_leaders.name: Franjo Tuđman
former_leaders.notes: HDZ founder; first president; led independence war; nationalist; authoritarian tendencies; died in office 1999; controversial (accused of partition deal with Milošević over Bosnia); 'Father of the Nation' for many Croats

910.name: Illyrian and Roman Dalmatia
910.description: The Illyrian and Celtic tribes of the Croatian lands, the Roman conquest of Dalmatia and Pannonia, and the enduring legacy of Roman urbanization including Diocletian's Palace at Split.

sub_clusters.name: Illyrian and Celtic Tribes
sub_clusters.description: The Illyrian tribes (Liburni, Delmatae) and Celtic Scordisci inhabiting Croatian territory, their seafaring traditions, and early encounters with Greek colonists.

sub_clusters.name: Roman Dalmatia and Pannonia
sub_clusters.description: Roman provincial administration, major cities like Salona (Solin) and Pola (Pula), Diocletian's retirement palace at Split, and the division between Western and Eastern Roman Empire.
key_events: Construction of Diocletian's Palace at Split (c. 305 AD)

920.name: Medieval Croatian Kingdom
920.description: The arrival of Croats in the Balkans, the formation of the Croatian Duchy and Kingdom, the reign of King Tomislav, and the eventual union with Hungary through the Pacta Conventa.

sub_clusters.name: Croatian Migration and Duchy
sub_clusters.description: The Slavic migration into former Roman Dalmatia and Pannonia, the Christianization of Croats, and the consolidation of Croatian duchies under Duke Branimir and others.

sub_clusters.name: Kingdom of Croatia and King Tomislav
sub_clusters.description: The crowning of Tomislav as the first King of Croatia (925), the unification of Pannonian and Dalmatian Croatia, and the kingdom's peak of independent power.
key_events: Tomislav crowned first King of Croatia (925)

sub_clusters.name: Decline and Union with Hungary
sub_clusters.description: The decline of the Croatian kingdom after the Trpimirović dynasty, succession crises, and the Pacta Conventa (1102) establishing a personal union with the Hungarian crown.

920.name: Croatia in Hungarian Union
920.description: Croatia as an autonomous kingdom within the Hungarian crown, the Croatian Ban as royal representative, the rise of the Croatian nobility, and Venetian control of the Dalmatian coast.

sub_clusters.name: Croatian Autonomy Under Hungary
sub_clusters.description: The functioning of the Croatian Sabor (parliament), the role of the Ban, Croatian noble families (Šubić, Frankopan), and the preservation of distinct Croatian legal traditions.

sub_clusters.name: Venetian Dalmatia
sub_clusters.description: The Republic of Venice's acquisition and governance of Dalmatian coastal cities, the cultural flourishing of Dubrovnik (Ragusa) as an independent maritime republic, and Italian-Slavic cultural exchange.

930.name: Ottoman Frontier and Military Border
930.description: Croatia as the 'Antemurale Christianitatis' (bulwark of Christendom) against Ottoman expansion, the devastating Battle of Krbava, the shrinking of Croatian territory, and the establishment of the Military Frontier.

sub_clusters.name: Ottoman Wars and Territorial Loss
sub_clusters.description: The catastrophic Battle of Krbava Field (1493), the Battle of Mohács (1526), the reduction of Croatia to 'remnants of the remnants of the once great and glorious Croatian Kingdom,' and the Croatian election of Habsburg rulers.
key_events: Battle of Krbava Field — devastating Croatian defeat by Ottomans (1493)
Croatian Parliament elects Ferdinand Habsburg as king after Mohács (1527)

sub_clusters.name: Military Frontier (Vojna Krajina)
sub_clusters.description: The Habsburg-organized Military Frontier (Vojna Krajina) as a permanent defensive zone, the settlement of Serbian Orthodox refugees as frontier soldiers, and the Zrinski-Frankopan conspiracy.

940.name: Habsburg Croatia and National Awakening
940.description: Croatia under Habsburg and later Austro-Hungarian rule, the Illyrian movement and Croatian National Revival, the struggle for autonomy within the Dual Monarchy, and the birth of South Slav (Yugoslav) political ideas.

sub_clusters.name: Habsburg Rule and Enlightenment
sub_clusters.description: The liberation of Croatian territory from the Ottomans after the Treaty of Karlowitz, Maria Theresa's centralizing reforms, and the beginnings of Croatian cultural and linguistic consciousness.

sub_clusters.name: Illyrian Movement and National Revival
sub_clusters.description: Ljudevit Gaj's Illyrian movement promoting South Slavic unity, Ban Jelačić's role in the 1848 revolution, and the struggle between Croatian autonomy and Hungarian Magyarization.
key_events: Ban Josip Jelačić abolishes serfdom and leads Croatian forces against Hungarian revolutionaries (1848)

sub_clusters.name: Croatia in Austria-Hungary
sub_clusters.description: The Croatian-Hungarian Settlement (Nagodba) of 1868, limited autonomy, the politics of Starčević's Party of Rights and Strossmayer's Yugoslavism, and Croatia's path toward the South Slav union.

950.name: Yugoslavia and World Wars
950.description: Croatia's experience within both Yugoslav states: the interwar Kingdom, the traumatic WWII Ustasha puppet state, Tito's communist Yugoslavia, and the rising nationalism that led to the breakup.

sub_clusters.name: Kingdom of Yugoslavia
sub_clusters.description: Croatian frustrations within the centralized Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, the assassination of Stjepan Radić, King Alexander's dictatorship, and the Cvetković-Maček Agreement.

sub_clusters.name: WWII: NDH and Ustasha Regime
sub_clusters.description: The Independent State of Croatia (NDH) as an Axis puppet state under Ante Pavelić, the Ustasha genocide against Serbs, Jews, and Roma at Jasenovac, and the Partisan resistance movement.
key_events: Establishment of the Ustasha puppet state NDH under Axis occupation (1941)

sub_clusters.name: Tito's Yugoslavia and Croatian Spring
sub_clusters.description: Croatia as a constituent republic of socialist Yugoslavia, economic development, the 1971 Croatian Spring reform movement suppressed by Tito, and the rise of nationalism after his death.

960.name: Croatian Independence and Homeland War
960.description: Croatia's declaration of independence, the devastating Croatian War of Independence (Homeland War), the siege of Vukovar, Operation Storm, and the reintegration of occupied territories.

sub_clusters.name: Independence and Siege of Vukovar
sub_clusters.description: Croatia's declaration of independence (June 1991), the JNA and Serbian paramilitary assault, the 87-day siege and fall of Vukovar, and the Vukovar massacre.
key_events: Fall of Vukovar after 87-day siege; Ovčara massacre (November 1991)

sub_clusters.name: Operation Storm and Reintegration
sub_clusters.description: Operation Storm (August 1995), the largest European land battle since WWII, recapturing the Republic of Serbian Krajina, the exodus of Croatian Serbs, and the peaceful reintegration of Eastern Slavonia.

960.name: EU Integration and Modern Croatia
960.description: Croatia's post-war democratic transition, EU accession negotiations, NATO membership, adoption of the euro and entry into the Schengen Area, and ongoing challenges.

sub_clusters.name: Democratization and ICTY Cooperation
sub_clusters.description: The post-Tuđman democratic transition, cooperation with the International Criminal Tribunal, EU accession negotiations, and the controversial trial and acquittal of General Ante Gotovina.

sub_clusters.name: EU Membership, Euro, and Schengen
sub_clusters.description: Croatia's EU accession (July 2013), adoption of the euro and entry into the Schengen Area (January 2023), economic modernization, and tourism-driven economic growth.
key_events: Croatia adopts the euro and enters the Schengen Area (January 1, 2023)

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
